_comment: Right Path — CONTACT HISTORY FACTS decision. Part of the established GoRules ZEN decision layer (same pattern as src/rules/next-best-action.json and src/rules/contact-options.json). This decision OWNS THE EMPLOYEE-FACING HISTORY WORDING for a single customer-contact change: given the normalized SHAPE of a change (a changeType plus the before/after presence of a value), it returns BOTH the classified changeKind AND the agreed wording as templates — the summary label and the one-line description sentence — so the phrasing lives here as data rather than being hardcoded in TypeScript. The TypeScript layer (src/lib/stewardship/contact-history-facts.ts) only substitutes two placeholders into the returned templates: {field} (the field label, e.g. Email / Phone / Date of birth) and {detail} (an optional trailing detail the layer supplies — the alert text for an alert, or the resulting email-availability state in plain words). No sensitive VALUE is ever fed to ZEN: ZEN sees only the shape, and the DOB day is never part of any template. ZEN never queries the database. 'first' hit policy: the first matching row wins. Changing the agreed wording is an edit to the templates in THIS file.

rules._description: A value field that had nothing before and has a value now: ADDED.
A value field that had a value and now has none: CLEARED (an empty value is a valid clear, never an error).
A value field that had a value and still has one, but a DIFFERENT one (the TS layer only emits a 'value' fact when the normalized value actually changed): CORRECTED.
A field's customer-verified confirmation cleared (a deliberate operator act, not the automatic clear that rides a value edit — the TS layer suppresses the automatic case before it reaches here).
A contact restriction turned ON (Do Not Text, Text Undeliverable).

The durable email-availability fact moved (e.g. to No Usable Email / Undeliverable / unknown). {detail} carries the resulting state in plain words; the TS layer suppresses the automatic 'available' that rides a saved usable email.
A customer alert added where there was none. {detail} is the actual alert text — the one place a value is shown, because the alert text IS the employee-facing fact.
A customer alert changed from one text to another. {detail} is the new alert text.
